summary: US President Trump announced via Truth Social that all mines in Strait of Hormuz international waters have been cleared or exploded, with Iran warned that any new mines will be destroyed immediately; the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier has departed Central Command area. Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi met his Omani counterpart in Tehran to finalize an interim shipping corridor agreement through Hormuz, with joint demining operations planned. Gaza tensions remain high as IDF struck five Hamas weapons storage facilities and a launch site embedded within mosques and humanitarian infrastructure, while kite/balloon attacks from Gaza continue unreported and unresponded since June.
key_points: Trump announced via Truth Social that the US Navy has cleared or exploded all mines in Strait of Hormuz international waters, warning Iran that any new mines will be destroyed immediately, with space forces monitoring every centimeter of the strait.

Iran and Oman have moved toward an interim agreement establishing a temporary shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz, with plans for joint de-mining and technical talks on permanent corridor management, potentially paving way for US-Iran negotiations.

IDF and Shin Bet struck and destroyed five Hamas weapons storage facilities and a launch site across multiple strikes in Gaza, with stored weapons including rockets, arms, explosives, grenades and combat equipment housed inside mosques beside humanitarian infrastructure.

Iranian economic indicators show dollar exchange rate reaching 205,000 tomans and gold coin at 224 million tomans, representing near 10% and 17% increases respectively within days, occurring one day after new US sanctions package announcement.
IDF Chief of Staff completed a visit to the Gaza Strip, meeting with combat troops and conducting operational assessment with commanders in the sector.
IDF struck a terror target in the village of Sarbin, South Lebanon, with artillery fire also reported on Kafr Rumman.
A grenade was thrown at a contractor's shop in Hadera, with large police forces responding to the scene.

Unit 595 conducted its first comprehensive battalion exercise in over three years, combining all teams from Syrian border to Lebanon border, operating under radar while collecting intelligence on targets.

sections.executive_summary: US forces have cleared mines from the Strait of Hormuz international waters following direct threats to Iran, while diplomatic efforts mediated by Oman have produced an interim shipping corridor agreement. Israeli forces conducted precision strikes on Hamas weapons facilities embedded within Gaza civilian infrastructure, with the IDF Chief of Staff visiting combat troops. Economic indicators show Iran's currency in freefall following new US sanctions.

points: Iran's dollar exchange rate reached 205,000 tomans on Tuesday, September 3rd, 1405, with the Imam coin trading at 224 million tomans—fresh records reflecting continued rial collapse and financial market turmoil one day after new US sanctions were announced.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met with Oman's Foreign Minister in Tehran to finalize an interim corridor arrangement through the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran's entry route and Oman's exit route for ships, alongside joint de-mining operations to restore maritime passage.

Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf publicly contradicted himself on X, first declaring 'Economic D-Day' then laughing and questioning why anyone would want to blow up the global financial system, showcasing internal incoherence in economic messaging.

Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Gharibabadi confirmed the Hormuz corridor agreement specifies Iranian waters for entry and Omani territorial waters for exit, with ships transiting through Iranian territory on both routes.
Iranian Foreign Ministry Desk threatened new measures against American interests if the US executes new sanctions, according to Reuters reporting via Israeli Channel 12.

President Trump stated Iran is not paying large portions of its military and is killing protesters—including those not protesting—in unprecedented numbers, characterizing the situation as a humanitarian crisis of enormous proportions requiring immediate action.

IDF and Shin Bet struck five Hamas weapons storage facilities and a launch site across multiple strikes in Gaza, destroying rockets, arms, explosives, grenades and combat equipment stored inside mosques and beside humanitarian infrastructure, warning that IDF will not accept any terrorism against Israeli civilians.
IDF Chief of Staff completed a visit to the Gaza Strip, meeting combat troops and conducting operational assessment with commanders in the sector amid ongoing responses to kite terror incidents.

Far-right MK Zvi Sukkot and others, under IDF escort, smashed a Palestinian monument in West Bank village of Madama, prompting IDF Spokesperson sharp condemnation of unauthorized action by the Knesset member contrary to coordination guidelines.

Unit 595 conducted its first comprehensive battalion exercise in over three years, unifying all teams from Syrian border to Lebanon border who normally rotate between sectors, operate under radar and collect intelligence on targets.
A grenade was thrown at a contractor's shop in Hadera, with large police forces responding; no casualties reported.

IDF reported June saw 9 kites launched against Israeli forces with zero reporting and zero response, while August recorded 12 kites and 4 balloons also with no reporting or response, citing Hamas use of incidents to drag Israel into intentional escalation.

Peace Council sent formal response to Gaza kite incidents stating all terror organization activities must cease including kite releases, and Israel must also honor ceasefire terms, with military action limited to responding to imminent threats only.

IDF struck five Hamas weapons storage facilities and a launch site across Gaza, with stored weapons including rockets, arms, explosives, grenades and combat equipment housed inside mosques and beside humanitarian infrastructure—cited as further evidence of Hamas cynical use of civilian sites.

Kite terror from Gaza continues unreported since June: 9 kites in June, and 12 kites plus 4 balloons in August, with IDF assessment identifying Hamas control of Gaza directing the launches to drag Israel into intentional escalation and blame.

Far-right MK Zvi Sukkot and companions smashed a Palestinian monument in West Bank village of Madama while under IDF escort, triggering IDF condemnation of unauthorized action using security forces for purposes beyond authorized scope.
Israeli forces raided the Skenaat area near Arab American University in West Bank, surrounding Sham housing complex, with no further details on outcomes or detentions reported.
Lebanese sources report IDF Air Force struck a terror target in the village of Sarbin, South Lebanon, marking a direct strike on a Hezbollah-affiliated position.
Artillery fire reported on Kafr Rumman in Lebanon, indicating ongoing kinetic exchanges along the northern border.

IDF Unit 595 conducted battalion-level exercises covering operations from Syrian border to Lebanon border for first time in over three years, suggesting expanded operational scope for intelligence and ground units.

Islamic Resistance Kataib Hezbollah issued statement condemning sentencing of Syrian Grand Mufti Sheikh Ahmed Badr al-Din Husun, describing it as continued targeting of Islamic figures who defended Islamic unity and moderation against sectarian projects.

Mazloum Abdi, commander-in-chief of Syrian Democratic Forces, announced official dissolution of SDF and all affiliated civilian and military structures during speech in Damascus, marking potential restructuring of Kurdish-led forces.
Egyptian Foreign Minister Abdelatty claimed Hamas agreed to hand over all weapons and stated Cairo is working to bring Iran back to negotiations, according to Persian-language reporting.

Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesperson stated US sanctions on Iran are unilateral and Qatar supports ongoing mediation efforts aimed at resolving the dispute, positioning Doha as intermediary between Washington and Tehran.

Armenia PM Nikol Pashinyan told parliament members Armenia will soon begin procedure to submit EU membership application, representing potential shift in South Caucasus alignment toward European structures.

key_developments: US Navy has cleared or exploded all mines in Strait of Hormuz international waters following direct presidential warning to Iran via Truth Social, with space forces monitoring every centimeter and zero-tolerance policy for new mining operations in effect.

Iran and Oman reached interim agreement establishing temporary shipping corridor through Strait of Hormuz with joint de-mining, with Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi meeting Omani counterpart in Tehran to finalize technical arrangements.

IDF and Shin Bet destroyed five Hamas weapons storage facilities and one launch site across Gaza in multiple strikes, targeting rockets, arms, explosives, grenades stored inside mosques and beside humanitarian infrastructure in civilian areas.
Iran's dollar exchange rate reached 205,000 tomans and Imam gold coin reached 224 million tomans—near 10% and 17% increases respectively—following new US sanctions announcement on Iran.

IDF Chief of Staff visited Gaza Strip combat troops and conducted operational assessment with sector commanders amid ongoing tensions from kite/balloon attacks continuing without IDF response since June.
Israeli Air Force struck terror target in Sarbin, South Lebanon with artillery fire on Kafr Rumman, representing direct kinetic action against Hezbollah-affiliated positions.

SDF Commander-in-chief Mazloum Abdi announced official dissolution of Syrian Democratic Forces and all affiliated civilian and military structures during Damascus speech, signaling major organizational restructuring.
sections.threat_assessment: The Strait of Hormuz de-mining represents a significant de-escalation of US-Iran maritime tensions, though Iranian threats of new countermeasures if sanctions proceed suggest instability remains. Israeli strikes on Hamas infrastructure in Gaza civilian buildings will likely generate international condemnation while eliminating weapons that threaten Israeli population centers. The continuation of unreported kite attacks presents an erosion of Israeli deterrence that Hamas may exploit for operational or diplomatic advantage. Lebanon border remains active with Israeli strikes on Hezbollah positions suggesting potential for northern front escalation.
sections.regional_response: Qatar continues positioning itself as mediator between US and Iran with explicit support for diplomatic resolution, while Oman has emerged as key diplomatic channel hosting both technical negotiations on Hormuz and bilateral talks. Egyptian Foreign Minister's claim of Hamas weapons handover agreement, if verified, could represent significant breakthrough in ceasefire negotiations. Armenia's announcement of imminent EU membership application signals potential realignment in South Caucasus with implications for regional security architecture.
sections.intelligence_notes: Iranian economic indicators show accelerated currency collapse with dollar gaining nearly 10% in days following sanctions, suggesting sanctions are biting but also increasing regime internal pressure. SDF dissolution announcement could disrupt US counter-ISIS operations and create security vacuum in eastern Syria requiring monitoring. IDF Unit 595 comprehensive battalion exercise indicates Israeli preparation for complex multi-front operations combining intelligence collection, ground maneuver and operational closure capabilities.
